features.label: Configure Country
features.description: Manage country config: identity, tax, logistics, commissions, payments, legal, regions, suppliers, payouts.
features.llm_description: This feature 'country.configure' allows for the configuration of country-specific settings within the application, including reading, writing, and approving changes. Given its high-risk designation, it involves direct manipulation of core domain logic and must be carefully managed to avoid potential data inconsistencies or security vulnerabilities.

features.label: Assign Country Staff
features.description: Assign/unassign users to a country with a country-scoped role (maker-checker required).

features.label: View Country Reports
features.description: Read country-scoped analytics and operational reports.
features.llm_description: This feature 'country.reports.view' allows users to view reports specific to different countries. Given its medium-risk classification, it primarily involves reading operations on country-specific data, which could potentially expose sensitive information if not properly secured, hence the need for careful implementation and possibly future feature gating.

features.label: Manage Country Tax
features.description: Draft and publish country tax rates and category tax rates.
features.llm_description: This feature 'country.tax.manage' allows users to read, write, and preview tax configurations for different countries, which is critical for financial operations but poses a high risk due to potential legal and financial implications if misconfigured. The domain code implementing this feature is not currently gated by any feature flag, meaning it will be fully active once deployed, requiring careful testing and validation.

features.label: Send Country Communication
features.description: List and send internal country communications; mark read.
features.llm_description: This feature 'country.communications.send' allows the system to send communications specific to a country's context. Given its medium-risk classification, it involves handling potentially sensitive data and must be implemented carefully to avoid security breaches or data leaks, especially during development and testing phases before full feature gating.

features.label: Approve Country Version
features.description: Approve/publish/rollback country config version drafts.
features.llm_description: This feature gate controls the approval process for country-specific version changes in the application, allowing read-only access to country versions, approving changes, publishing them, and rolling back if necessary. Given its high-risk nature, it ensures that only authorized personnel can approve and publish critical updates, preventing potential issues that could affect multiple regions or users.

features.label: Manage Country Payout Rules
features.description: Manage country payout rule categories and products.
features.llm_description: This feature gates the ability to manage country-specific payout rules, including reading existing rules, creating new ones, and deleting outdated rules. Given its high risk, it must be carefully implemented and thoroughly tested to prevent unauthorized access or data corruption in critical financial operations.

features.label: Manage Country Localization
features.description: Manage numeral system, RTL layout, address format, holidays, delivery zones.
features.llm_description: This feature gates the ability to manage country-specific localization settings within the application, including reading and writing localized data for different countries. Since the risk is low and the feature is currently not gated by any specific requirement checks, it can be implemented with minimal impact on existing functionalities, though careful testing of internationalization aspects is necessary.

features.label: View Cross-Border Sessions
features.description: View cross-country customer sessions and conversion tracking.
features.llm_description: This feature 'country.cross_border.view' allows users to view cross-border sessions within the application. Since it is currently labeled as low-risk and only involves read actions, there are minimal security concerns, but proper access controls should still be implemented to prevent unauthorized data access. The domain code that supports this feature has not yet been integrated with any feature-gating mechanisms, meaning all users have unrestricted read access to cross-border session data for now.

violations.finding: 27 files bypass the module→domain composition rule by importing from the deprecated controllers layer (e.g. domains/accounts/services/user_read_service.py, domains/country/services/user_read_service.py, domains/customers/services/user_read_service.py).
violations.action: Route logic must live in module routers; business logic must live in domain services.

violations.finding: 213 module routers carry business logic / DB writes (e.g. customer/addresses.py; customer/cart.py; customer/coupons.py; customer/customer_coupons_create.py; customer/customer_coupons_mgmt.py).
violations.action: Push logic into domain services; routers keep only auth + require_feature + one call.

violations.finding: 117 module routers have no feature/auth gate at all (e.g. logistics/parcel_tracking.py; supplier/product_moderation.py; supplier/product_verification.py; supplier/product_videos.py; supplier/supplier_bg_ab_test.py).
violations.action: Every router endpoint must include require_feature(...) or equivalent auth dependency.

violations.finding: 3822 cross-domain imports bypass the sanctioned ports/events path (e.g. accounts → audit (core.py), accounts → comms (core.py), accounts → comms (core.py)). Allowlist entries: 27.
violations.action: Route cross-domain reads through the target domain's ports.py or read_models/; route cross-domain writes through events.py/subscribers.py only.

violations.finding: 13/18 domains have an empty features.py (no atoms): accounts, catalog, infrastructure, media, hr, orders, analytics, payments, security, logistics, _parked, comms, audit.
violations.action: Seed each domain's feature atoms so the rbac catalog is complete and single-sourced.

violations.finding: 1 require_feature(...) literals are NOT in any domain features.py (e.g. customers.customer.read).
violations.action: Add the missing atom to the owning domain's features.py or fix the literal (CI must fail).

violations.finding: 7 ORM model classes omit an explicit Postgres schema in __table_args__ (e.g. promotions.py::BOGOPromotion, media_models.py::MediaUploadSession, employee_models.py::EmployeeRiskScore, employee_models.py::PayrollRecord, employee_models.py::TrainingModule).
violations.action: Declare __table_args__ = {'schema': '<domain>'} so each domain owns one DB schema.

violations.finding: 285 ORM model classes have a non-plural snake_case table name (e.g. core.py::Cart, core.py::CartItem, user.py::User, user.py::UserLoginHistory, user.py::UserDevice).
violations.action: Rename to plural snake_case (e.g. CountryConfig → country_configs).

violations.finding: 76 ORM model classes omit the country_code column (e.g. user.py::SocialIdentity, country_basics.py::CountryBasics, country_enhancements.py::OmanDeliveryZone, core.py::UserBrowsingHistory, core.py::SystemHealthEvent).
violations.action: Add country_code as an independent RLS scope axis on every business table.

violations.finding: 131 ORM model classes omit created_at/updated_at (e.g. core.py::Address, core.py::CartItem, user.py::UserLoginHistory, user.py::UserDevice, user.py::PasswordResetToken).
violations.action: Add created_at and updated_at to every business table.

violations.finding: 184 ORM model classes omit is_deleted (e.g. core.py::Address, core.py::Cart, core.py::CartItem, user.py::UserLoginHistory, user.py::UserDevice).
violations.action: Add is_deleted to every business table for soft-delete compliance.

violations.finding: _legacy/ folder absent — no deprecated shims tracked.
violations.action: Keep DOMAIN_ALLOWLIST.yaml shrinking to zero.
